name: TcrToken/Tecra pool unauthorised USDT drain
summary: TcrToken.burnFrom checked and reduced _allowances[msg.sender][from] instead of _allowances[from][msg.sender]. A caller could therefore approve the pool as a spender of the caller's balance, burn TCR directly from the pool without the pool's authorization, synchronize the depleted TCR reserve, and exchange previously acquired TCR for the pool's USDT.
notes: Direct TcrToken deployment. Archival code is empty immediately before block 12231755 and the deployed runtime hashes to 0x5936633a992a28ec4c8685b5d4e7e0f10ac1fd7cee088c0e07b2eb043e6757a8 both in the creation block and immediately before the exploit. Although TcrToken has a custom optional legacy-upgrade route, deprecated was false and upgradedAddress was zero immediately before the incident, so burnFrom executed in this unchanged direct runtime.

The exploit receipt records exactly 639,222.253258 USDT transferred from the TCR/USDT pair to the attack helper. The helper's initial 0.04 ETH route supplied 112.863254 USDT to the pair before the burn. Excluding that identifiable campaign input leaves the exact pre-recovery victim depletion of 639,109.390004 USDT recorded here; financing costs and later recovery are not subtracted.
